lean_source:
namespace Pipeline.Generated

/-- POSIX slash test. -/
def isSlash (c : Char) : Bool := c = '/'

/-- POSIX basename algorithm on the character list of the pathname.
    Step 1: a null string stays null (GNU prints an empty line).
    Steps 2-3: a string of only slashes (including "/" and "//") becomes "/".
    Step 4: trailing slashes are removed (dropWhile on the reversed list).
    Step 5: everything up to and including the last remaining slash is
    removed (takeWhile non-slash on the reversed list). -/
def basenameChars (cs : List Char) : List Char :=
  if cs.isEmpty then []
  else if cs.all isSlash then ['/']
  else ((cs.reverse.dropWhile isSlash).takeWhile (fun c => !isSlash c)).reverse

def basenameStr (s : String) : String := String.ofList (basenameChars s.toList)

set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
/-- One PATH operand: print its basename, exit 0. Anything else is outside
    the modeled scope: no output, exit 1 (an error occurred).
    `stdin` is deliberately unused: POSIX says STDIN is not used. -/
def run (args stdin : List String) : List String × UInt32 :=
  match args with
  | [p] => ([basenameStr p], 0)
  | _ => ([], 1)

/-- EXIT STATUS: successful completion is 0 for any single operand. -/
theorem run_exit_success (p : String) (stdin : List String) :
    (run [p] stdin).2 = 0 := rfl

/-- STDOUT: exactly one line is written for a single operand. -/
theorem run_single_line (p : String) (stdin : List String) :
    (run [p] stdin).1.length = 1 := rfl

/-- STDIN: not used — the result is independent of standard input. -/
theorem run_ignores_stdin (p : String) (s t : List String) :
    run [p] s = run [p] t := rfl

/-- Step 3: a nonempty string consisting entirely of slash characters
    (e.g. "/", "//", "///") produces exactly "/". -/
theorem run_all_slashes (p : String) (stdin : List String)
    (hne : p.toList ≠ []) (hall : p.toList.all isSlash = true) :
    (run [p] stdin).1 = ["/"] := by
  have hemp : p.toList.isEmpty = false := by
    cases h : p.toList with
    | nil => exact absurd h hne
    | cons a as => rfl
  show [basenameStr p] = ["/"]
  simp only [basenameStr, basenameChars, hemp, hall, Bool.false_eq_true,
    if_false, if_true]

/-- Membership in takeWhile implies the predicate holds. -/
theorem mem_takeWhile_pred (q : Char → Bool) :
    ∀ (cs : List Char) (c : Char), c ∈ cs.takeWhile q → q c = true := by
  intro cs
  induction cs with
  | nil => intro c h; simp [List.takeWhile] at h
  | cons a as ih =>
    intro c h
    by_cases ha : q a = true
    · rw [List.takeWhile_cons, if_pos ha] at h
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp h with rfl | hmem
      · exact ha
      · exact ih c hmem
    · rw [List.takeWhile_cons, if_neg ha] at h
      simp at h

/-- Steps 4-5: when the pathname is not entirely slashes, the resulting
    string contains no slash character (it is the last pathname component). -/
theorem run_output_no_slash (p : String) (stdin : List String)
    (hnotall : p.toList.all isSlash = false)
    (c : Char) (hc : c ∈ ((run [p] stdin).1.headD "").toList) :
    c ≠ '/' := by
  have hemp : p.toList.isEmpty = false := by
    cases h : p.toList with
    | nil => rw [h] at hnotall; simp [List.all_nil] at hnotall
    | cons a as => rfl
  have hout : ((run [p] stdin).1.headD "").toList
      = ((p.toList.reverse.dropWhile isSlash).takeWhile (fun c => !isSlash c)).reverse := by
    show (basenameStr p).toList = _
    simp [basenameStr, basenameChars, hemp, hnotall, String.toList_ofList]
  rw [hout, List.mem_reverse] at hc
  have := mem_takeWhile_pred (fun c => !isSlash c) _ c hc
  simp [isSlash] at this
  exact this

/-- dropWhile leaves a list unchanged when no element satisfies the predicate. -/
theorem dropWhile_eq_self_of_none (q : Char → Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List Char, (∀ c ∈ cs, q c = false) → cs.dropWhile q = cs := by
  intro cs h
  cases cs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons a as =>
    rw [List.dropWhile_cons, if_neg]
    simp [h a (List.mem_cons_self ..)]

/-- takeWhile keeps a whole list when every element satisfies the predicate. -/
theorem takeWhile_eq_self_of_all (q : Char → Bool) :
    ∀ cs : List Char, (∀ c ∈ cs, q c = true) → cs.takeWhile q = cs := by
  intro cs
  induction cs with
  | nil => intro _; rfl
  | cons a as ih =>
    intro h
    rw [List.takeWhile_cons, if_pos (h a (List.mem_cons_self ..))]
    rw [ih (fun c hc => h c (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hc))]

/-- Content preservation: a nonempty pathname containing no slash at all is
    its own basename — the operand is echoed unchanged. -/
theorem run_no_slash_identity (p : String) (stdin : List String)
    (hne : p.toList ≠ []) (hnos : ∀ c ∈ p.toList, isSlash c = false) :
    (run [p] stdin).1 = [p] := by
  have hemp : p.toList.isEmpty = false := by
    cases h : p.toList with
    | nil => exact absurd h hne
    | cons a as => rfl
  have hnotall : p.toList.all isSlash = false := by
    cases h : p.toList with
    | nil => exact absurd h hne
    | cons a as =>
      have := hnos a (by rw [h]; exact List.mem_cons_self ..)
      simp [List.all_cons, this]
  show [basenameStr p] = [p]
  have hrev : ∀ c ∈ p.toList.reverse, isSlash c = false := by
    intro c hc
    exact hnos c (List.mem_reverse.mp hc)
  have hdrop : p.toList.reverse.dropWhile isSlash = p.toList.reverse :=
    dropWhile_eq_self_of_none isSlash _ hrev
  have htake : p.toList.reverse.takeWhile (fun c => !isSlash c) = p.toList.reverse :=
    takeWhile_eq_self_of_all _ _ (by intro c hc; simp [hrev c hc])
  simp [basenameStr, basenameChars, hemp, hnotall, hdrop, htake,
    String.ofList_toList]

end Pipeline.Generated

spec_theorems.name: run_exit_success
spec_theorems.informal: EXIT STATUS: with a single string operand, basename exits 0 (successful completion) for every input.

spec_theorems.name: run_single_line
spec_theorems.informal: STDOUT: basename writes exactly one line to standard output for any single operand.

spec_theorems.name: run_ignores_stdin
spec_theorems.informal: STDIN: not used — the output and exit code are independent of standard input.

spec_theorems.name: run_all_slashes
spec_theorems.informal: Step 3: a nonempty string consisting entirely of slash characters (e.g. "/", "//", "///") results in the single string "/".

spec_theorems.name: run_output_no_slash
spec_theorems.informal: Steps 4-5: when the string is not entirely slashes, the resulting string contains no slash character, i.e. it is the last pathname component after trailing slashes and the directory prefix are removed.

spec_theorems.name: run_no_slash_identity
spec_theorems.informal: Content preservation: a nonempty string containing no slash is its own last pathname component and is written unchanged.
